g.text: The concept ladder: each rung answers the question the last one leaves open
A suggested order for a reader with zero prerequisites.
1 Packet, address, port, protocol
How does data find a program?
2 Network, router, route, hop
How does it cross networks?
3 Private addresses, NAT, IPv6, CGNAT
Why can't my friend reach me?
4 Port-forward / relay / VPN -> tunnel
How can two NATed PCs talk? (define "encapsulation" here)
5 Tailscale: STUN, hole punching, DERP, TUN, MTU
Now every PC has a reachable address.
6 Containers: namespaces, cgroups, veth, bridge
How do two containers on ONE host talk?
7 Cluster: node, manager, worker, service, task, ports
How do containers on DIFFERENT hosts talk?
8 Overlay + VXLAN: VTEP, FDB, ARP proxy, MTU
What exactly would Docker Desktop have to provide?
9 Docker Desktop / WSL2: documented vs hypothesis
So which setup works?
10 Hands-on + verification script
Does it really work? Prove it.
Left: reachability (the networking you need before any container). Right: containers, Swarm, the overlay, then the real setup.
